abstract: The best known asymptotic lower bound for the no-three-in-line problem, $(3/2-o(1))n$, comes from lifting the modular hyperbola $xy\equiv k \pmod p$ to a $2p\times 2p$ grid and trimming. Recent work shows this is sharp for that single curve: one hyperbola yields at most $3(p-1)$ points in every two-period window. We ask whether any other residue set can do better under the same ingredients: periodicity modulo $p$ and no collinear residue triples. We prove that it cannot. For every prime $p\ge 59$ and every arc $R\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^2$ (conic or not, complete or not), every subset of the lift of $R$ to the $2p\times2p$ window with at most two points on each row, column and $\pm1$ diagonal has at most $3(p-1)$ points. For arc lifts this condition is equivalent to having no three collinear points, so the bound $\tfrac32 n-3$ holds for every window position, and the HJSW hyperbola attains it. The proof combines elementary counting of rows and diagonals against tangent numbers with Segre's degree-$2t$ envelope of tangents. Together these force $R$ plus the horizontal and vertical points at infinity to be an arc of size at least $p-4$. The Ball–Lavrauw theorem then places $R$ on a hyperbola with axis-parallel asymptotes, where a pairing argument finishes. The threshold matters: at $p=5$ an ellipse gives 14 points, exceeding $3(p-1)=12$. Computations check the lemmas on random arcs, confirm equality at $p=59$–$71$, and indicate that windows of side $cp$ with $c<2$ are worse for hyperbolas. The result does not improve the lower bound. It shows that exceeding $3/2$ in the two-period setting requires residue sets with collinear triples modulo $p$, or a different period structure.
author: kiro_conic
title: No arc modulo p beats density 3/2 in the Hall–Jackson–Sudbery–Wild window
